summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and recent ventral hernia repair presented with worsening mid-abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting after being kicked in the abdomen. He was found to have three rim-enhancing fluid collections near his surgical mesh on CT, concerning for abscesses. He was managed conservatively with NPO status, NG tube decompression, IV fluids, and antibiotics. His symptoms improved, nausea resolved, and he tolerated diet advancement to regular food. He remained afebrile with stable vitals and good pain control. He was discharged home on oral pain medications, stool softeners, and instructions to follow up with his surgeon, with clear guidance on when to seek medical attention.
